name: Permanent residence permit (tidsubegrænset opholdstilladelse)

requirement_groups.name: Standard track: 8 years' residence, 2 of 4 supplementary conditions

requirements.blocker_text: Requires 8 years of continuous legal residence in Denmark, all basic conditions (age 18+, no criminal record, no debt to public authorities, no receipt of benefits under the active/integration law, full-time employment or self-employment for approximately 4 years within the last 4.5 years, income at or above a set annual threshold, and passing a Danish-language test at Prøve i Dansk 2 or equivalent), plus at least 2 of 4 supplementary conditions.
requirements.fix_path: Continue accruing continuous legal residence toward 8 years, and secure at least 2 of the 4 supplementary conditions (higher Danish test level, extended full-time employment, sustained higher income, or active civic engagement).

requirement_groups.name: Accelerated track: 4 years' residence, all 4 supplementary conditions

requirements.blocker_text: The 8-year requirement is halved to 4 years for applicants who meet all 4 of the supplementary conditions rather than only 2 -- including a higher Danish-language level (Prøve i Dansk 3 or equivalent) and an extended full-time employment record (roughly 3.5 years within the last 4), on top of all basic conditions.
requirements.fix_path: Meet all 4 supplementary conditions (rather than 2) to access the accelerated 4-year track.

evidence_required.document: Proof of 8 (or 4) years' continuous legal residence
Danish-language test certificate (Prøve i Dansk 2, or Prøve i Dansk 3 for the accelerated track)
Employment/self-employment history documentation and income records

outcome.duration_length: indefinite (residence card itself is periodically reissued, but the underlying status does not expire)

sources.title: Nyidanmark.dk (Udlændingestyrelsen) -- Ansøg om permanent opholdstilladelse, confirming the 8-year/4-year structure and the 2-of-4/4-of-4 supplementary-conditions mechanism directly

notes: SOURCING UPGRADE, a genuine tier-1 catch: this route is built directly against a fetched nyidanmark.dk page, confirming Denmark's 8-year/4-year dual-track structure with unusual precision -- the standard track requires all basic conditions plus at least 2 of 4 supplementary conditions after 8 years, while meeting all 4 supplementary conditions (rather than only 2) halves the residence requirement to 4 years, a real, deliberate policy design rewarding stronger integration markers with materially faster settlement, correctly modeled here as two genuinely distinct requirement_groups rather than one blended rule. This is among the most demanding permanent-residence regimes documented in this dataset by raw residence-year count -- 8 years as the default, compared to 5 years in Poland, Korea's F-5, or Italy's EU long-term residence, and matched or exceeded only by China's investor tracks' multi-year holding periods and Saudi Arabia's 10-year naturalisation floor -- though Denmark's accelerated 4-year track brings it closer to the dataset's more common 4-5 year norm for applicants who can meet the full supplementary-conditions bar. The income and employment thresholds referenced in the basic conditions (approximately DKK 280,908/year as of a 2018 figure cited in one corroborating source) are adjusted periodically and the current 2026 figure was not independently confirmed against a primary source in this research pass -- flagged as a follow-up target, since this specific number is likely stale given multi-year gaps between citations. citizenship_after_months (24) reflects the standard 2-year permanent-residence-to-naturalisation-eligibility window; refugees and stateless persons qualify for a reduced 1-year window instead, but that reduction is modeled on dk_naturalisation directly (where it is now tier-1 sourced) rather than duplicated here as a third PR-track group, since it doesn't change the permanent-residence grant itself -- only how soon naturalisation becomes available afterward.
